tagline: High desert, Joshua trees, and a road named for a camp.
intro: Highway 247 leaves Route 66 country at Barstow as Barstow Road and heads south through the Ord Mountains and past Lucerne Dry Lake to Lucerne Valley. There it becomes Old Woman Springs Road and runs southeast along the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains, through Johnson Valley and Homestead Valley, past Black Lava Butte and Flattop Mesa to Yucca Valley. Along the way are Joshua trees, cholla and creosote bush, and few power lines or billboards.
The name goes back to 1856, when a survey party came on elderly Native women camped at a spring here while the young went into the mountains for pinyon nuts.

moments.title: Ord Mountains
moments.text: A 14-mile desert range on public land, topping out at 6,309 feet on Ord Mountain, with the Ord Mountain Trail through one section.

moments.title: Lucerne Lake
moments.text: A dry lake bed in the Mojave nearly four miles long and five across at its widest, east of Apple Valley.

moments.title: Landers
moments.text: Gold prospectors settled it from 1914, and from the late 1940s through the 1970s UFO enthusiasts gathered here for conventions. The magnitude 7.4 earthquake of 1992 was centered here.

sources.label: Scenic America, California designates State Route 247 as its newest scenic byway
